articles.title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Rugby and cricket among sports dropped from scaled-down event
articles.summary: The 2026 scaled-down Commonwealth Games will take place from July 23 to August 2; Glasgow, which hosted the event in 2014, stepped in to stage the event after the Australian state of Victoria withdrew last year; athletics and swimming are included as compulsory sports
articles.body:
The scaled-down Games will take place from July 23 to August 2, the Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF) announced on Tuesday.

Glasgow, which hosted the event in 2014, stepped in to stage the event after the Australian state of Victoria withdrew last year.

The Games will feature a 10-sport programme across four venues within an eight-mile corridor, with more than 500,000 tickets made available for spectators.

Athletics and swimming are included as compulsory sports for 2026, while there will also be track cycling, gymnastics, netball, weightlifting, boxing, judo, bowls and 3x3 basketball.

There will also be integrated para events in six of those sports - athletics, swimming, track cycling, weightlifting, bowls and basketball.

Among the sports missing out compared to the 2022 Games in Birmingham are triathlon, diving, hockey, T20 cricket, squash, badminton and rugby sevens.

Commonwealth Games Scotland chair Ian Reid said it was not easy to decide which sports to include.

"I think everybody recognises that these events need to be more affordable, lighter and we would have loved to have all of our sports and all of our athletes competing but unfortunately it's just not deliverable or affordable for this time frame," Reid said.

However, he thinks the sport programme will start to vary and may increase in size depending on venues in future cities, so there is a chance more sports may again be included.

Around 3,000 athletes are expected to compete from up to 74 Commonwealth nations and territories representing a combined total of 2.5 billion people - a third of the world's entire population.

The four venues confirmed to host events are Scotstoun Stadium, Tollcross International Swimming Centre, Emirates Arena - including the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome - and the Scottish Event Campus.

It is estimated the Glasgow 2026 Games will deliver more than £100m of inward investment into the city.

Athletes and support staff will be housed in hotel accommodation.

Scotland's First Minister John Swinney said: "As well as an action-packed, inclusive sports programme that will inspire and excite audiences across the globe - Glasgow 2026 will also be a cultural celebration.

"I would like to thank Commonwealth Games Scotland for their hard work and dedication to produce a viable proposal for Glasgow 2026 - and to the Commonwealth Games Federation and Commonwealth Games Australia for their assistance in helping to secure the Games."

articles.title: Australia 56-17 Japan: Wallabies seal series as 1,000th cap recipient scores on debut
articles.summary: Australia wrap up two-Test series win with eight-try victory over Eddie Jones’ Japan; Japan remain winless against Wallabies in nine Tests, stretching back to 1975; watch the entire South Africa vs New Zealand Test series live on Sky Sports from August 22
articles.body:
Prop Taniela Tupou scored a double before his replacement, De Lutiis, scored on debut to mark becoming the 1,000th Wallaby with his first international try.

Six of Australia's eight tries were scored by front-row forwards, with hooker Josh Nasser, loosehead Angus Bell and replacement hooker Brandon Paenga-Amosa all getting on the scoresheet.

Flanker Charlie Cale and skipper Harry Wilson chipped in with late scores, while scrum-half Ryan Lonergan and replacement fly-half Ben Donaldson combined to kick all eight conversions.

Japan scored first-half tries through Harry Hockings, Naoto Saito and Dylan Riley but were kept pointless after the break as their losing streak against Australia, which dates back to 1975, extended to nine Tests.

Australia took an early lead twice via tries from Josh Nasser and Tupou, but Saito and Ryunosuke Ito supplied quick ball to regularly expose holes in the Wallabies defence as Japan rallied both times.

Lock Hockings charged down a poor attempted exit from Lonergan at the base of a ruck and dived on the ball in goal, while Saito took a quick-tap penalty and darted over from close range.

Japan took the lead in the 33rd minute through Australian-born Dylan Riley, who beat two tackles and reached over for a try, but Australia hit back before the break via a line-out move from which Tupou crashed over.

De Lutiis came on in the 50th minute to replace veteran prop Tupou, who barged over for two first-half tries, and was on the shoulder of Angus Bell a minute later as his fellow front-rower scored to give Australia a 26-17 lead.

De Lutiis scored himself in the 58th minute, backing up in support at the perfect time after an Australian attacking raid that started with fly-half Carter Gordon breaking the defensive line and running 30 metres towards the right corner flag.

That try and a conversion from scrum-half Ryan Lonergan, his fifth, gave Australia an 18-point cushion with 20 minutes remaining after a tightly contested first half in which Japan's surprising line speed in defence and enterprising, relentless attack unsettled the Wallabies.

Three late tries helped the Wallabies turn a 21-17 half-time lead into a 39-point victory, giving the Australians a three-match winning streak for the first time since 2024.

The Wallabies beat Italy last month in the Nations Championship in Joe Schmidt's last match as head coach, before a 35-32 win over Japan in Osaka last weekend in Les Kiss' first game in charge.

articles.title: South Africa vs New Zealand: Springboks captain Siya Kolisi not selected for first Test against All Blacks
articles.summary: South Africa and New Zealand renew rugby's 'Greatest Rivalry' in the first match of their four Test series at Ellis Park this Saturday; watch South Africa vs New Zealand live on Sky Sports Action on Saturday from 4.10pm
articles.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus named the inexperienced Paul de Villiers in his matchday squad ahead of Kolisi, who has been nursing a hamstring injury sustained in their 17-10 victory over Argentina on August 8.

With three further Tests against the All Blacks to come in Cape Town, Johannesburg and Baltimore, USA, Kolisi has not been risked.

"Siya trained well with us this week, and although we could have selected him for this clash, we thought it would be best to select Paul," Erasmus said.

"We are playing four Tests against the All Blacks and Paul has been playing well, so we are excited to give him a chance this weekend in what will be his first Test match against New Zealand, while taking a precautionary approach to Siya's return.

"We have a solid group of players, and each one of them deserves their place in the squad, so we will approach team selection week by week."

Centre Damian de Allende will earn his 100th Test cap at Ellis Park, becoming the 10th player in South African rugby history to reach the century landmark.

Fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and lock Eben Etzebeth are the only players to retain their starting positions from the victory in Buenos Aires.

Prop Ox Nche, meanwhile, starts for the first time since July's Nations Championship victory over England.

South Africa have won five of their last six Tests against New Zealand, including inflicting a record 43-10 defeat on their great rivals in Wellington last September.

"They are a quality team and they're very well coached, so we are preparing for an 80-minute grind," Erasmus added.

"They have a well-rounded squad with physical forwards and an exciting backline, so we have to be sharp and accurate in our execution from the outset.

"Many of the matches between the sides have come down to the wire, so it's important that we use the chances we create and ensure that our discipline is on point.

"It's going to be a big battle, but the entire squad is excited about the match and looking forward to it."

Savea, Roigard, Jordan start for New Zealand

Ardie Savea, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan all start for New Zealand in Saturday's first Test.

Captain Savea, scrum-half Roigard and record try-scoring wing Jordan will make their first appearances of this summer's tour of South Africa, while full-back Damian McKenzie returns after injuring his ankle in the warm-up victory over the Sharks in Durban.

Head coach Dave Rennie has blended experience with youth, with 110-cap duo Savea and Codie Taylor facing the Springboks for the 18th and 17th time respectively, while Anton Segner and Josh Moorby will face South Africa for the first time.

"After all the build-up and anticipation, our whole touring squad is excited to get this first Test underway," Rennie said.

"We have selected a balanced mix of big-match, experienced players and younger players who have earned the right to play in this first Test.

"The first three franchise games have exposed our newer players to the way South African teams play and have been fantastic in helping us build combinations and develop the game we want to play.

"We know the Test series will be a huge step up. We're well aware of what the Springboks will bring to the contest and the pressure that will come to bear.

"They are No 1 in the world, playing at their spiritual home in front of their passionate fans, so we will have to be at our very best on Saturday."

articles.title: South Africa vs New Zealand: All Blacks emerge worthy winners as they outscore Springboks in first Test upset
articles.summary: South Africa lose their first game at home since August 16 2025 after a huge second half from New Zealand sees them pull away from the Springboks to claim a 33–16 victory at Ellis Park and take the opening Test of the series
articles.body:
The Boks led 13-12 at half-time, but New Zealand took over in the second half to close it out and end South Africa's unbeaten streak.

The All Blacks had ​been underdogs going into the first international of their eight-match tour ​but took full ⁠advantage of the ⁠home side's numerous handling errors and ill discipline ‌for a statement victory that ended a 12-match winning streak for ‌the Springboks and will rock the confidence of the world champions.

"I'm incredibly proud, the score might be convincing but there was nothing in it and it ​was an absolute arm wrestle," said winning coach Dave Rennie.

"We defended and defended and we were clinical when we got our ⁠opportunities. It's a great result for us,"

Will Jordan extended his run as ⁠New Zealand's record try ​scorer with two tries that ​bookended scores from Josh ​Moorby, Fabian Holland and Luke ⁠Jacobson.

Ruben Love kicked over four conversions.

South Africa's try came ⁠from Andre Esterhuizen with ​three penalties and a conversion ​from Cheslin Kolbe but they lost their discipline towards the end, after multiple turnovers, and finished with 13 players as Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sent to the ‌sin bin in the final 10 minutes.

"In hindsight there were two or three big moments where we let the game get away from us because New Zealand forced us into ‌errors by being intense and sharp," said coach Rassie ​Erasmus.

The series moves to sea level in Cape Town next Saturday and New Zealand are now the surprising front-runner in the first full series between the teams in 30 years.

articles.title: South Africa vs New Zealand: Siya Kolisi, Handre Pollard return as Springboks look to level Test series in Cape Town
articles.summary: Siya Kolisi, Handre Pollard, Cobus Reinach and Ethan Hooker drafted into much-changed Springboks XV ahead of Saturday's must-win second Test against the All Blacks; watch South Africa vs New Zealand live from 4.55pm on Sky Sports Action and Sky Sports +
articles.body:
The back-to-back reigning world champions surrendered top spot in the rankings to the All Blacks after Saturday's shock 33-16 defeat, their heaviest home loss to New Zealand.

The Springboks travel to Cape Town for the second instalment in the first four-Test series between the two sides in 50 years knowing only a victory will keep their hopes of winning alive.

Coach Rassie Erasmus has responded defeat in Johannesburg by making four changes to his starting XV and bringing five fresh faces onto the replacements bench.

Kolisi will start at flanker providing the hamstring issue which ruled him out of the first Test doesn't resurface during training. If he remains unfit, Paul de Villiers will retain his position at No 7.

The Springboks coach highlighted Kolisi's value at the breakdown and in organising South Africa's defensive structure alongside Pieter-Steph du Toit, areas he felt were lacking in the first Test.

"Paul played well on Saturday and there's no reason why we should keep him out, but Siya is our captain," Erasmus said.

Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been dropped to the bench and Manie Libbok omitted from the matchday 23 as double World Cup winner Pollard forms a new half-back pairing with Cobus Reinach. Ethan Hooker replaces the injured Cheslin Kolbe on the wing.

"Handré has delivered for us under extreme pressure," Erasmus said of Pollard, who kicked South Africa to World Cup glory in 2019 and 2023.

The bench includes Deon Fourie, Thomas du Toit, Lood de Jager, Cameron Hanekom and Morne van den Berg. Fourie could become South Africa's oldest Test player at 39 if he features, surpassing Victor Matfield and Schalk Brits.

articles.title: New Zealand's tour of South Africa: All Blacks come from behind to beat Lions 41-35 after huge scare in tour match
articles.summary: New Zealand fight back from 18 points down to beat the Lions and remain unbeaten on their tour of South Africa, who they beat in the first Test of their three-match series - watch the second Test live on Sky Sports Action and Sky Sports + from 4.55pm on Saturday
articles.body:
It means that the All Blacks have swept all four provincial teams to remain undefeated on their six-week, eight-match tour of South Africa, on top of beating the Springboks 33-16 in ​the first Test at the weekend.

New Zealand fielded only three players from that Saturday Test victory over South Africa on the same ground and involved five injury replacements summoned on tour - including one who arrived on Monday - as well as giving a debut to prop Saula Ma'u.

Their defence struggled and missed 19 tackles over the course of the contest that saw them trail 14-0 after seven minutes.

They were still behind at half-time and 35-17 behind in the 47th minute, as the Lions threatened to become the first South African provincial side to beat New Zealand since Orange Free State, now known as the Cheetahs, in 1976.

But like the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls who the All Blacks had already beaten, the Lions are out of season and not match fit.

Having not played since May 30 in the United Rugby Championship quarter-finals, New Zealand eventually came storming back in the last 30 minutes with four successive tries.

Rieko Ioane scored two of them, flanker Ethan Blackadder went over for a second time to earn the All Blacks the lead for the first time in the 62nd minute, while a second too by winger Emoni Narawa in the 79th finally settled the touring side's nerves.

"The Lions came out hissing," Blackadder said. "But we stayed composed and found a way in the end. They were quality tonight."

Blackadder - whose father Todd was on the last traditional tour in 1996 - was one of the New Zealand standouts along with inside center Timoci Tavatavanawai, Narawa, and fly-half Richie Mo'unga, back from Japan and in a black jersey for the first time since the 2023 World Cup final.

All Blacks coach Dave Rennie thought Blackadder was phenomenal. "He's got a massive engine and was everywhere," he said.

Blackadder's Test prospects also improved after Anton Segner was ruled out of the rest of the tour.

Segner was a late withdrawal from the first Test reserves due to an ankle injury that's needed two surgeries. The injury was assessed as acute inflammatory arthritis and he won't be replaced in the squad.

Mo'unga, like New Zealand, got better as the game got older, but he and Beauden Barrett could convert only three of the team's seven tries.

On the other hand, Chris Smith, at home, converted all five of the Lions tries and hit the post with a long penalty.

articles.title: South Africa vs New Zealand: Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie’s war of words escalates as series hangs in the balance
articles.summary: The four-match South Africa-New Zealand series is level at 1-1 ahead of the third Test, with head coaches Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie embroiled in a war of words over scrum tactics; watch every minute of New Zealand's tour of South Africa exclusively live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Picture the scene: The touring All Blacks win the opening Test with a 33-16 at Ellis Park . Then, the Springboks hit back with a thrilling 33-26 victory over New Zealand in Cape Town .

Named in the front row for the Springboks for that contest were Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw. Just one hour before kick-off, that was changed to Gerhard Steenekamp, Deon Fourie and Thomas du Toit with the original three dropping to the bench.

Erasmus said this was down to conditions and a chance of rain not materialising.

"We thought it was going to be wet and that's why we picked the front row, Erasmus said after the match. "The whole weather prediction, the whole week, was it was going to be wet."

On this matter, Rennie refused to criticise.

"We stuck with the team we named and it doesn't worry me at all," Rennie said on the matter.

"They named their team on Monday. That had no bearing on the team that we named. So, yeah - no drama from my perspective."

It is important to note that, under World Rugby regulations, medical dispensation is usually required for a team to be permitted to be make changes within 48 hours of the game kicking-off.

However, with Rugby's Greatest Rivalry independently administered, Erasmus can chop and change as much as he pleases.

In total, Erasmus made five changes from the squad he named on Monday for the second Test, including a complete change to the front row. During the week, Handre Pollard went from fit to injured and was eventually withdrawn, while Cheslin Kolbe went from injured to fit and was ultimately named on the wing.

That is why he is keeping it under his hat ahead of the third Test in Johannesburg - if conditions require it, of course.

"If it's clear and dry this will be the team that's starting, but if it rains we might make a change or two," Erasmus said.

Scrum disagreement erupts: 'Don't come with that nonsense'

While there have been no real arguments over late changes, with diplomacy reigning supreme, one issue that has erupted is a disagreement over scrums.

Rennie has accused the Springboks of "walking around" during scrums, alleging they are illegally angling sideways rather than staying square and driving straight. He believes this gives them an unfair advantage by allowing them to get around the All Blacks' front row.

The New Zealand head coach is so irked by the issue that he said he had provided feedback to World Rugby.

"The scrums were better tonight. I think the referee [Angus Gardner] was pretty strong around setting a mark and trying to keep hookers in the same sort of space. The Springboks moved across further left and he stopped them," Rennie said.

"We will give a bit of feedback around that. It is still a bit of an issue for us because they are able to walk around and then go straight through our tighthead.

"There are a couple of little technical things we will share, again, but I thought at the end, both teams were able to play off them. So, I think Angus did a reasonable job there."

Of course Erasmus responded to Rennie's comments saying "don't come with that nonsense" in a fired-up response.

"We've been playing with the pack of these guys together. It's the first time ever in history that people are talking about us walking around. Why would we, all of a sudden, walk around?

"I wouldn't come with that nonsense and say we are walking around and try to put those things out in the media. If I'm starting to put things out, the last lineout was skew and we contested. I'm not going to moan my a--- off about that.

"If they just want to start moaning about stuff like that, then they are under pressure."

Is it pressure? Is it mind games? Whatever it is, it has set the stage for a third Test that promises to be even spicier, more dramatic, and a further reminder of why this series was dubbed Rugby's Greatest Rivalry.

articles.title: South Africa vs New Zealand: Cape Town stadium low jet flypast probed by South African aviation authority
articles.summary: South Africa's aviation authority is reviewing a low flypast by two passenger jets, with plans for another flyover withdrawn; watch every minute of New Zealand's tour of South Africa exclusively live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) said it had obtained flight data recordings and requested additional information from Airlink as part of its assessment into the incident involving two passenger jets which passed within 100 metres of the DHL Stadium roof on Saturday.

A full report with recommendations will be issued once the review is complete.

"It is therefore critical that we interrogate this past weekend's events … to determine if there were any safety concerns which warrant a review," the agency said in a statement.

Airlink has withdrawn plans for another flyover at the upcoming rugby match in Soweto, according to the SACAA, which is responsible for regulating aviation safety and security.

The flyover ahead of the Springboks-All Blacks rugby match on August 29 drew huge cheers from an estimated crowd of about 56,000 but also sparked a debate over the safety risks after video footage by spectators inside and around the stadium spread online.

Airlink on Wednesday said the manoeuvre had been carefully planned and rehearsed and that safety was "the first consideration at every stage of the process."

It said each aircraft had three senior captains aboard, with more than 75,000 combined flight hours across the crews.

Earlier this week, Airlink had provided the data from the airplanes' black boxes to the civil aviation authority for review.

The SACAA said it would examine flight data to determine whether any safety concerns warranted a review.

The airline acknowledged the enthusiasm generated by the spectacle while also recognising what it described as the "valid questions and concerns" that followed.

"We never intended to become the news or upstage Rugby's Greatest Rivalry," said Airlink chief executive de Villiers Engelbrecht.

The regulator said the airline had made applications for three flyovers. The most recent one in Cape Town was the second, while the first flyover took place in Johannesburg on August 22. Both were approved in line with the requirements for special air events.

Airlink has withdrawn its application for a flyover scheduled for September 1, over Johannesburg's FNB Stadium.

The airline said forecast weather conditions were unfavourable for a safe formation flyby. SACAA confirmed that the application had been withdrawn.

South African rugby has a long tradition of stadium flybys at major matches, dating back to the 1995 Rugby World Cup final in Johannesburg, when a Boeing 747 swept over Ellis Park before the Springboks faced the All Blacks.

Last Saturday's flyby was unusually low and dramatic, drawing international attention, with some aviation experts later questioning whether the aircraft had left too little margin for error.

articles.title: England rugby squad: Courtney Lawes and Joe Marchant told to ‘go above’ Gallagher Prem rivals to earn spot back
articles.summary: The England internationals have returned to the Gallagher Prem but were left out of Steve Borthwick’s side’s recent camp; Courtney Lawes and Joe Marchant have five competitive fixtures to play themselves into the autumn squad
articles.body:
Steve Borthwick recently named his squad for his three-day camp that started on Sunday, with Lawes and Marchant left out despite their return to the Gallagher Prem with Sale Sharks making them eligible for selection.

It was understood the England head coach wanted to see how the pair, who had been playing for French clubs Brive and Stade Francais respectively, got on before handing them a spot back in the team.

Now, defence coach Richard Wigglesworth has confirmed they are waiting to see how the pair fare on their return to England's top flight.

"We want as much quality as we can have in the league but they are going to have to go and play well," Wigglesworth said when asked about centurion Lawes and useful midfield option Marchant.

"There are some good players in the room and to pick them you have to leave someone else out, so they would have to go over and above that I would say.

"It's great to have Courtney back. He has unbelievable experience, is an England legend and has been flying in pre-season, as everyone is.

"There is a real excitement about watching him back in the Prem, so I'm enjoying that.

"I have actually bumped into Joe Marchant walking around living quite close to me, so I caught up with him and it is great to have him back."

Rugby union rules state only players who compete in the Gallagher Prem can be selected, meaning both players have put themselves back into contention.

Lawes retired from international rugby after the 2023 World Cup, but his return to home soil has raised hopes that he could feature at the 2027 World Cup in Australia at the age of 38.

"Everyone's case is individual in where you want to play your rugby and what you want to do," Wigglesworth said. "I couldn't have given up the chance of England because I didn't play as much as loads of people.

"But Courtney has said 'I've got an itch here and I'm coming back'. How good is that as a statement? 'I am coming back because I want to do this'.

"That level of determination and the qualities he has should put himself in a good spot. Experience, he has certainly got that. We are keen to watch him play."

The Nations Championship begins on November 6, with England taking on Australia on November 8.

articles.title: England 48-15 Australia: Red Roses' seven-try second-half blitz earns win in WXV Global Series opener
articles.summary: Seven tries in the second half saw England open their WXV Global series with a win over Australia; Next, England meet Canada in a repeat of their 2025 World Cup final at Sandy Park in Exeter on September 19; they round off the home leg of the series against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium
articles.body:
Despite a scintillating second 40 from the hosts, the first half was all about Australia as they showed defensive strength to hold on to a 10-5 lead at half-time thanks to a Samantha Wood penalty and a converted Faliki Pohiva effort.

When Wood was in the sin bin for a deliberate knock on was the only time the Red Roses got on the board as Abi Burton went over from short range. Holly Aitchison was unable to add the extras.

Remarkably, it was the first time the Red Roses had trailed at half-time in seven years, the last time coming all the way back in 2019.

However, it was in the second half that England got back to their usual best and with tries from May Campbell, Meg Jones, Bryony Field, Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer, Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, plus a conversion from Holly Aitchison and three from Zoe Harrison, they made it 39 matches in a row unbeaten.

The Wallaroos did get a second-half try thorugh Eva Karpani, who was earlier sent to the sin bin for an infringement in the build-up to Venner's try but it was merely a consolation as the Red Roses showed just why they are currently the No 1 ranked team and world champions.

Next up for England is Canada on September 19 in Exeter, before they face New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on September 26.

A second-half serving of Red Roses running wild

It was truly a tale of two halves in the North West of England as Australia took an early lead after England were penalised for holding on, Wood slotting over the conversion for a three-point lead after four minutes.

The Red Roses thought they had quickly hit back through skipper Meg Jones but on review, she was offside as the charge down on the kick occurred and so her effort was chalked off, and the visitors' early advantage was reinstated.

Despite Australia taking control, they allowed England to get into the game when Wood was sent to the sin bin for a deliberate knock on and they had to battle for 10 minutes with just 14 players.

They did well for five minutes until the Red Roses' numerical advantage brought the spoils on the left edge, Sadia Kabeya passing back on the inside to send Burton in.

That did not deter Australia though and back at full strength, they thought they had gone over through Brittany Merlo but once again the video referee intervened and this time dismissed the try due to sealing off at the line-out.

It took eight minutes for the Wallaroos to go over again and this time it was from an impressive steal at the line-out. Off the back of it, Pohiva used her strength to burrow over and Wood converted to put Australia 10-5 ahead.

Australia's defence, as it did throughout the majority of the first half, then continued to stand firm and deny England any more points before the break. That meant they went in behind for the first time in seven years and were firmly in unprecedented territory.

That seemed to motivate the home side though and it took seven minutes for England to pull the line-out maul out of their back pocket with Campbell finishing it off. This time, Aitchison converted for a 12-10 lead.

Four tries in 10 minutes saw England find their electric best in attack and take the game away from Australia.

On the 51st minute, skipper Jones finished off a brilliant Aitchison kick. On the 55th minute, debutante Field steered the driving maul over. On the 57th minute, Venner went over in the corner and then on the 61st minute, Kabeya forced her way over under the posts to cap off a relentless period.

This time, Harrison added the conversion to put England 34-10 up with less than 20 minutes remaining.

During that pressure, things went from bad to worse for Australia as they had Karpani sin-binned for an infringement during the build-up to Venner's try and of course, England were not done adding points to their tally.

Replacement No 7 Packer then got in on the actions as she used the breakdown in her favour to get over, Harrison accurate with the boot once again to put the Red Roses 41-10 up.

On her return from a 10-minute sit down, Karpani did manage to hit back for Australia as she crashed over from the back of the lineout.

However, England made sure to have the last word as Moloney-MacDonald showed her speed on the edge, Harrison capping off the afternoon with a brilliant touchline conversion to see the game finish 48-15.

Player of the Match Abi Burton told BBC Sport:

"It was tough, they made us work for it. We knew we weren't at our best at half-time, we needed to come out and bring it to them physically because they came out absolutely gunning.

"That cohesiveness started to click at the end. There is so much more to come from this team, we've just got a few teething issues to sort out.

"It's going to take time for us to get back into it with a shorter pre-season. But it's about how we adapt quickly and great ready for the next Test match.

"We're a different group of players in some aspects, but the messages have always been the same: be the best versions of ourselves and be as cohesive as possible. It's an ever-evolving Red Roses team."

articles.title: Wheelchair Super League Grand Final: Halifax Panthers beat Leeds Rhinos 64-24 to become double treble winners
articles.summary: Standout performances from Jack Brown and Rob Hawkins helped Halifax Panthers recover from going 8-0 behind early on and claim another triumph in the Wheelchair Super League Grand Final
articles.body:
The Rhinos initially took an 8-0 lead thanks to tries from an impressive Nathan Collins at the Belle Vue Leisure Centre in Manchester.

But the Panthers, inspired by brilliant performances from Jack Brown and Rob Hawkins, began to show their class.

Rhinos couldn't shut down the pace of Brown and Hawkins, who regularly stormed through to help make it 34-8 at the break.

Conversions from Wayne Boardman also helped keep the opposition at bay.

Rhinos showed spirit in the second half but the Panthers were ultimately too good before finishing 64-24 winners.

They become back-to-back treble winners after winning the Betfred Challenge Cup and Betfred Wheelchair Super League League Leaders' Shield and title for two consecutive seasons.

Last year, the Panthers' win over the London Roosters was intensely physical and brutal with Mason Billington becoming the first player to be sin-binned in a Wheelchair Super League Grand Final as a brawl threatened to erupt.

But while this year's contest didn't threaten to break out into violence, it was still played with high intensity, summed up by Brown sawing metal off his own chair at half-time after suffering damage.

Repairs were a regular feature in the match, further demonstrating its physicality.

Earlier this week, Hawkins was announced as part of a three-man shortlist for the 2026 Wheels of Steel trophy at the Rugby League Awards Night on 29 September.

London Roosters star Joe Coyd and Rhinos' Tristan Norfolk were also nominated.

England star Coyd is the reigning Wheels of Steel winner.

Roosters star Max Owen has been named Young Player of the Year after the Scottish international made his debut in July last year.

Martyn Gill from Edinburgh Giants was named Coach of the Year.

articles.title: Women's Lions tour a 'top goal' for Wales prop Sisilia Tuipulotu
articles.summary: Wales prop Sisilia Tuipulotu says selection for next year's inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour is among her top rugby priorities.
articles.body:
Wales prop Sisilia Tuipulotu says selection for next year's inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour is among her top rugby priorities.

The in-form tight-head scored two tries in Wales' emphatic 50-19 victory over South Africa on Friday, under the watchful eye of Lions head coach Jo Yapp.

With Yapp saying she will only take the best players in each position, most of the touring party to New Zealand is expected to be made up of England's world cup-winning stars.

But Tuipulotu's barnstorming display certainly puts her on the radar for when the squad is announced in May.

"I actually didn't know she [Yapp] was there until after the game, but I'm very happy that we gave the performance that we did in front of her," said Tuipulotu.

"It's probably number one on my goal list right now, to perform the best I can to put my hand up for a spot on that team."

One year until first women's Lions Test - will it be a success?

Wales deliver performance of serious promise

Tuipulotu, 23, exploded onto the international scene in the 2023 Six Nations, where she earned her "prop idol" nickname.

But injuries and potentially a lack of confidence amid Wales' slump in form never saw her reach the heights of her early promise.

But fans saw the Tuipulotu of old on Friday, with former Wales centre Jonathan Davies calling her performance "world class" during punditry.

Tuipulotu, who joined Harlequins from Gloucester-Hartpury in the summer, credits the six weeks of pre-season for getting her back to her best shape.

"This is probably the best place where I could be physically," she said.

"In the last year I've come back from injury, but I haven't played the rugby that I wanted to play, so I'm happy with how Friday went."

Live on BBC One, iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app, with live text coverage

Wales' attention now turns to USA, who they face at Cardiff Arms Park on Saturday (15:00 BST).

USA pulled off a stunning comeback victory against Ireland on Sunday, and are now up to sixth in the world, while Wales have risen two places to 11th.

"We'll go into this game confident," said Tuipulotu.

"We're going into this game with a win in hand, but to back it up even more will just give us that fire in our bellies to go out and perform.

"If we just carry on playing the way we do and improve every week, then hopefully we get the crowd there too."

articles.title: From Odisha’s villages to the Asian Games: The stories behind India’s women’s rugby squad
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Kolkata: Odisha’s rugby pipeline continues to power the Indian women’s sevens programme, with four players from the state earning selection in the squ.
articles.body: Kolkata: Odisha’s rugby pipeline continues to power the Indian women’s sevens programme, with four players from the state earning selection in the squad for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.Senior campaigner Dumuni Marndi (Mayurbhanj) will feature in her second Asian Games alongside Mama Naik (Keonjhar), Nirmalya Rout (Bargarh) and Sandhyarani Tudu (Baripada, Mayurbhanj).For Marndi, the selection marks another chapter in a journey that began in rural Mayurbhanj, where her sporting ambitions were initially met with resistance at home.Asian Games Full Coverage| Schedule | Medal Tally“The last Asian Games was a huge learning experience. At that time, there were so many seniors around me that I could just focus on playing. Now there is more responsibility because I’m one of the senior players,” said the vice-captain.The quartet’s inclusion is the latest testament to Odisha’s enduring influence on Indian rugby, with Sandhyarani Tudu among a long line of players to emerge from the state’s thriving grassroots system. She took up the sport after coaches introduced rugby at her school and believes Odisha’s strong culture has been central to its success.“Rugby is doing very well in Odisha. We consistently win medals and our team bonding is very strong. That has helped many players come through,” said Sandhyarani, a fly-half known for her tackling, passing and game awareness.Former age-group captain Mama Naik has also emerged as one of India’s brightest forward prospects, while Nirmalya Rout adds leadership credentials after captaining Odisha to the 2026 senior nationals crown.But even as Odisha continues to produce national team regulars, the sport is spreading across newer regions as well. Bihar, for instance, has two players in the squad.One of them is Arti Kumari, who continues to draw inspiration from her elder brother Rahul Kumar, who died in an accident in 2020.“My brother was my biggest supporter. He always encouraged me to chase my dreams,” said Arti, who hails from Nawada.Fellow Bihar player Guriya Kumari, from Muzaffarpur, has overcome a very different challenge. The youngster battled back from an ACL injury that required two surgeries on the same leg.“There was a time when I thought I would never be able to play again,” Guriya recalled.However, she has put all that behind her and is focused on the Asiad, where India will play its Pool B opener against Hong Kong on Oct. 1 at Paloma Mizuho Rugby Stadium. India's remaining two pool games will be against defending champions China and Malaysia.While head coach Paul Delport expects a stern test at the Asian Games, he is taking confidence from India’s recent performance at Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series, where the team finished sixth after recording victories over UAE and Iran. India also had a preparatory camp in Thailand, where they played practice matches against the hosts and Sri Lanka.“The players have improved enormously, both physically and in terms of game understanding. Considering how few tournaments we’re able to play, the progress has been exceptional,” Delport said of the team that finished seventh in the last Asiad.The former South Africa international, however, insisted that the focus must remain on the process rather than the results. Rugby India president Rahul Bose also echoed that sentiment, arguing that progress in team sports often takes longer to become visible on the scoreboard.But with an eye on the 2032 Olympics, Bose reiterated the need to create a more professional ecosystem for players.“We have to make rugby fully professional. You cannot just have camps and send players home. Centres of excellence and year-round programmes are the way forward,” he said in Kolkata on Monday.While Bose hinted that some of those plans could begin taking shape in the coming months, the immediate focus remains the Asian Games for which the team departs on Friday.The squad: Shikha Yadav (C), Dumuni Marndi (VC), Amandeep Kaur, Arti Kumari, Bhumika Shukla, Vaishnavi Patil, Guriya Kumari, Kalyani Patil, Mama Naik, Nirmalya Rout, Sandhya Rai, Sandhyarani Tudu, Ujjwala Ghuge.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Henry Pollock: England flanker extends deal with Northampton
articles.summary: Henry Pollock has brought an end to his contract stand-off with Northampton, saying it was ultimately "a very easy decision" to sign an extension.
articles.body:
Henry Pollock has brought an end to his contract stand-off with Northampton, saying it was ultimately "a very easy decision" to sign an extension with the defending Prem champions.

"I am very, very happy to sign here," Pollock told BBC Radio Northampton.

"I have been here my whole career so it made sense for me to stay on the journey with such a young group of players, who are so ambitious.

"It was a very easy decision in the end."

The 21-year-old forward's new terms tie him to Northampton until the summer of 2028, raising the prospect of talks restarting in around a year's time.

Pollock, whose profile has exploded over the past two seasons after appearing for England and the British and Irish Lions, had been talked up as a "seven-figure player" during negotiations by his advisor Eddie Hearn.

However, the boxing promoter's valuation was never likely to be met at Northampton or elsewhere in the Prem, given Saints' star-studded line-up, the league's £6.4m squad salary cap and rules over players moving between clubs.

The exact level of Pollock's pay increase is unclear. While some sources have valued his new contract at £400,000 a year, others involved in the deal say the figure is higher.

His salary is certainly short of Scotland playmaker Finn Russell, who, as Bath's marquee player, is on the league's most lucrative package, worth about £1m a year.

Pollock's pay puts him well ahead of most of his contemporaries in the Prem, however.

His new deal is comfortably ahead of the average annual salary in the league (£191,000), the average earned by someone in his 20-22 age bracket (£106,000) and with his level of international experience (£224,000), as revealed by the latest league payroll data, covering the 2024-25 campaign. , external

Only 4% of Prem players that season were paid in excess of £400,000 a year.

Pollock's previous contract, signed in December 2024, is understood to have been worth about £150,000.

"I don't create it, my team do," said Pollock of the speculation that has surrounded his future over the past seven weeks.

"It is one of those things that you have to take in your stride, but I am happy it is all done and I can focus on the rugby."

Asked about the possibility of Saints becoming the first side since Saracens in 2019 to successfully defend their English title, Pollock was bullish.

"We have the squad depth and the belief in this group that we can do it," he said.

"Let's see, hopefully we can create some magic along the way. Let's write a new story."

Pollock, who was instrumental in Northampton's run to the title last season, insisted last week that he was still open to offers, raising the possibility of a move abroad or even to another sport.

However, remaining at Northampton, for whom he made his league debut in November 2023, always seemed the most likely option.

After winning an age-grade world title with England's under-20s at the end of that season, Pollock returned to Franklin's Gardens and established himself as a first-team regular.

Saints news and views from BBC Radio Northampton

His pace, energy and on-pitch persona propelled him into the public consciousness and into contention for international honours.

He made his Test debut off the bench against Wales, scoring two tries, in March 2025 and was a bolter pick for the Lions squad only two months later.

His try-scoring feats through Saints' run to the Champions Cup final, complete with pre-planned celebrations, earned him a spot on the eight-strong shortlist for the continental competition's player of the year.

He has appeared in each of England's past 12 Tests, albeit with his only start coming in a 42-21 defeat by Ireland in February.

"Over the last few years, everyone has seen the quality he brings on the pitch and the speed of his rise through the game – but just as importantly, he's a young man of outstanding character," said Northampton's director of rugby Phil Dowson.

"What's most exciting is that there's still so much more to come from him. Henry is incredibly ambitious and constantly looking for ways to improve. He understands that individual success comes from contributing to a successful team, and he's already taken on leadership responsibilities within the squad despite his age.

"People sometimes underestimate how intelligent he is as a rugby player. When we sit down to review performances, he's often identified the same things we were going to discuss before we've even raised them. His understanding of the game is excellent, and that gives him a huge platform to keep progressing.

"He's become an important figure not just for Saints, but for the wider game. He inspires young supporters, brings excitement to rugby, and understands that everything off the pitch is built on performing consistently on it. We're excited to see what he can achieve over the coming years."

articles.title: Henry Pollock: England star signs new multi-year deal with Northampton Saints to stay with defending PREM champions
articles.summary: Henry Pollock's contract with Northampton Saints had been due to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season; the England international previously said he was open to exploring all options over his future
articles.body:
Pollock has been a key part of the Saints side since bursting through as a 17-year-old in 2022, delivering a Player of the Match performance during their Gallagher PREM final victory last season.

The back rower already has 13 England caps and five British & Irish Lions caps to his name, with his growing appeal seeing him become the first rugby player to join Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency earlier this year.

Pollock previously said he had an open mind about next steps in his career, with Hearn labelling him worth at least £1m a year, but the 21-year-old is now looking forward to extending his time at Saints.

In a statement, Pollock said: "I'm massively happy to re-sign with Saints, my boyhood club. It's an exciting place to be right now. We're in a great spot as a team, but it feels like there's still so much more growth in us.

"I'm still young, and we've got a young squad with a brilliant group of lads. Some of my best mates are here, and every day everyone pushes each other to improve and be the best players and team we can be. For where I am in my career, this is exactly where I want to be.

"I feel like we're only just getting started. We won the PREM last season and we want to go again. Winning the Champions Cup is another huge ambition for us. We came so close a couple of years ago, and achieving that together would be incredibly special.

"I just want to enjoy every moment of this journey. I'm playing for my boyhood club, surrounded by great people, and that's something I never take for granted. The connections within this group are what make it such a special place."

Saints' Director of Rugby, Phil Dowson, added: "We're delighted that Henry has committed his future to Saints.

"Over the last few years, everyone has seen the quality he brings on the pitch and the speed of his rise through the game - but just as importantly, he's a young man of outstanding character.

"Keeping someone with both his talent and mindset is hugely important for the club."

'Rugby not used to Pollock and Hearn's contract posturing'

"Henry Pollock's transfer stand-off with Northampton divided the club's fanbase. The England flanker is a generational talent. The friction wasn't just financial - it was also cultural.

"Rugby isn't used to the sort of public posturing that Pollock and his agent Eddie Hearn have engaged in over this new deal. It's very un-rugby. Very un-gentlemanly.

"Some will say that the sport and the attitude of its fans need to evolve. Others will say these are the core values that drive people to play, watch and fall in love with the game.

"The new £400,000-plus contract is likely to represent a three-fold increase in Pollock's salary and make him one of the top-earning flankers in the Premiership.

"It's not the seven-figure sum Hearn thinks his client is worth - but within the parameters of the league and its salary cap, it's an excellent deal. The 21-year-old has the potential to become one of the sport's all-time greats, but he's not there yet."

articles.title: Marlie Packer chats to Sky Sports about England's Red Roses  losing their winning run, planning a response vs New Zealand and motherhood
articles.summary: After England's Red Roses lost their 39-Test winning run dating back to 2022 last week in a 26-26 draw vs Canada, experienced back-row Marlie Packer speaks exclusively to Sky Sports ahead of WXV Global Series Test vs New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham this Saturday (3pm kick-off)
articles.body:
Last week, Canada took their first step towards avenging Rugby World Cup final defeat to England by ending the Red Roses' record winning streak - dating back to 2022 - in a gripping 26-26 draw in Exeter.

Eight days short of the one-year anniversary of England's 33-13 World Cup final triumph at Twickenham, the sides treated a sold-out Sandy Park to an absorbing WXV Global Series clash featuring eight tries that went down to the final play with the clock in the red.

Speaking to Sky Sports on Tuesday, experienced back-row Packer - 2023's World Player of the Year - said New Zealand can expect a Red Roses backlash at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Saturday.

"For us, obviously, it's not what we wanted, but it wasn't a loss. It's a learning curve," Packer said.

"It's made us put even more work into this week and focus on New Zealand come Saturday.

"I think it sharpens the mind, but also just shows we are human.

"It was an arm wrestle, and Canada brought it to us. It was a great game. It was the World Cup final last year and we played again now. But it's a three-Test series. We're now going to play them out in Canada twice.

"For us, it's about making sure we learn from that draw. We'll learn, and we'll do better next time.

"Most definitely [no better way to respond than beating New Zealand]. Playing at the home of English rugby, every player wants to play there.

"There's literally a new pitch as well there for us, so I'm really excited for that. The girls are buzzing just to get back out there.

"New Zealand can expect a very strong Red Roses team coming at them.

"The fact is we're not a team that worries about what happened last week. We're looking forward and we're looking forward to this game.

"They're going to see a very happy, strong Red Roses team coming in to put on a show for the fans, but also a performance for ourselves.

"I think they're going to be a very strong, dynamic New Zealand team, but we're a very dynamic, strong Red Roses team.

"So for the fans and for the neutral, it's going to be another great game of rugby."

Also on the horizon for Packer is the arrival of her second child, with fiancée and Red Roses team-mate Rosie Galligan due to give birth at the end of next month.

Due to that fact, Packer confirmed she is planning to step away from rugby for a period once the baby arrives.

"I'm really excited. It's five weeks until Rosie [Galligan] has our little girl.

"We're so excited, but for me, it's head into New Zealand this week, and then I can start getting really excited for baby girl to come.

"I won't be going away to Canada for the away leg, I'll be staying here and supporting from the sideline.

"I'll be supporting and cheering on the girls and I'm sure I'll be back on the phone to Mitch [head coach John Mitchell] a couple of times."

'Edwards wanting to work with us shows where women's rugby is going'

Earlier this week, news emerged former Wales, British and Irish Lions and France defence coach Shaun Edwards had joined the England Women coaching team as a consultant until the end of the WXV Global Series.

Packer believes the appointment points to the progress women's rugby and the Red Roses specifically have made in recent years.

"He's [Edwards] been excellent," Packer said. "He's been in the last couple of days.

"He's got an amazing CV, hasn't he? I think he's won more Six Nations than all of us.

"He's coming in to coach defence and he says it how it is. He's just a great coach to have in.

"And actually, for us to have him until the end of this WXV period, and how wanted to come in and coach women and get involved, is amazing for us.

"It just really shows where the game is going, but also where the women's game for Red Roses is, when coaches of his calibre want to be a part of us.

"It's defence day today, so we've heard his voice! We've learned a couple of new tricks that he's coached us."

articles.title: Henry Pollock: Eddie Hearn says back row 'left money on the table' with Northampton deal
articles.summary: Henry Pollock turned down rival offers worth much more than his Northampton extension, which will earn him over £400,000 a year, says adviser Eddie Hearn.
articles.body:
Henry Pollock turned down rival offers worth hundreds of thousands of pounds more than his extension to stay at boyhood club Northampton, says Eddie Hearn.

Hearn, whose Matchroom promotional empire is centred on boxing, darts and snooker, has been working as Pollock's adviser since March.

Pollock, 21, has agreed a new deal with Saints that extends his terms to summer 2028 and is worth more than £400,000 a year.

"There were a couple of domestic offers – a couple of Prem offers - and international offers as well," said Hearn of Pollock's options during his renegotiation.

"We had a very, very straight conversation. I said to him, 'be honest, do you want to go?' And he went, 'no, I really don't want to go'. And that was it.

"He knew the numbers, but ultimately he just wanted to stay at the club.

"He left a lot of money on the table to stay with Northampton. But it wasn't even a tough decision for him."

Hearn says that some of Pollock's suitors were offering "well in excess of seven figures".

The £1m mark was where Hearn valued Pollock's annual salary prospects in an interview with the Daily Telegraph interview in August. , external

Hearn acknowledges that his client's new deal "didn't quite get to the number" that was targeted.

The headline basic figure Pollock has accepted does not account for a signing bonus and various payments he receives for off-pitch work.

And Hearn says that Pollock's endorsement deals have carried him comfortably over £1m in total annual earnings.

"Everybody from major financial institutions to household brands to performance brands to nutritional brands to wellness brands… I mean, there isn't really a sector that hasn't hasn't approached us about Henry Pollock," said Hearn.

Pollock is keen to explore the possibility of representing Great Britain in rugby sevens at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

GB's qualification is far from certain after the programme went part-time and the team slipped from the top tier of the international circuit.

The back row's new deal does not include the sort of dedicated time to train up for sevens that France captain Antoine Dupont took before Paris 2024, but the prospect has been raised with Saints.

"Our principal obligation is to perform for Northampton and to help them win championships," said Hearn.

"Part of the arrangement allows him to look at those kind of opportunities, but only with a sensible conversation with the club."

'If Matchroom did rugby, it would be a stroll in the park'

Pollock's ability to maximise his on-pitch earnings in England is restricted by a £6.4m salary cap for Prem clubs.

Each team is allowed one player whose salary is exempt from the calculations; however, players who move between top-tier teams can only qualify for such marquee status after two years with their new side.

"Let the players earn," he said. "All they hear about is salary caps or one star player per team - marquee names or whatever you want to call it. You don't want that.

"You want to say to a young player, 'hey, come to rugby, you can be a superstar and you can earn a fortune'.

"You could have lost Pollock and it would have been a disaster for English rugby."

The salary cap is designed to make the Prem sustainable and competitive, with similar systems in place in most major American sports.

Players such as Pollock can supplement club earnings with a central England contract, worth about £150,000 a year, or one-off Test match fees.

Still, some England players, such as Jack Willis, Kyle Sinckler and Sam Simmonds, have left for France's Top 14 where a salary cap of 11m euros (£9.4m) offers scope for greater earnings.

Hearn's current stable of rugby stars is only two strong. Bath and Scotland fly-half Finn Russell is similarly represented by Matchroom in off-pitch matters and advised by Hearn.

However, Hearn has ambitions to become more deeply involved in the staging and promotion of the game. He is set to meet with Prem Rugby chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor in Monaco in the coming weeks to discuss ideas.

"We haven't really touched the surface in terms of what we could do in the sport," said Hearn.

"All I've done is done a few deals with Henry, he's come to a couple of fights and I've done a couple of Zoom calls [with journalists].

"That just shows you the buzz that can be created with a little bit of hype and perception.

"But hype and perception are nothing without substance. The sport and the brand is the substance and it's significant in rugby.

"Look at what Matchroom has done elsewhere. Boxing was dead, darts was non-existent, snooker was stuck in the air. We don't fail. Our track record is second to none.

"If we went into rugby, it would be a stroll in the park for me. It's a huge global sport steeped in history with fantastic values and tradition that just needs to be just turbo-charged."

articles.title: Scarlets 'ready to come out fighting' amid uncertain future - Davies
articles.summary: Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies says talk about the organisation's long-term future has galvanised his squad before the new season starts this weekend.
articles.body:
Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies says talk about the organisation's long-term future has galvanised his squad before the new season starts this weekend.

The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has outlined how it plans to cut from four men's professional teams to three by 2028, with Ospreys and Scarlets set to fight to be the side in west Wales.

The governing body says the decision will be made in time for the 2028-29 season, with one side in the capital, one in the east and one in the west.

WRU-owned Cardiff and Dragons, an independently backed business, are set to be given licences in the capital and east respectively.

That leaves Swansea-based Ospreys and Llanelli-based Scarlets to compete for the spot in the west, with a merger currently being ruled out.

"The situation has energised us," said Davies.

"It's typical Welsh, isn't it? You put us in the corner and we come out fighting."

WRU sticking to three-team plan - Reddin

Scarlets vow to remain at heart of west Wales

Scarlets chief Daniels dismisses Ospreys merger

History and facilities favour Scarlets - Davies

The WRU has stated the process to decide the framework for the final decision will begin in December and finish before the end of the 2026-27 season.

So eyes will be on the results and attendances of Ospreys and Scarlets in this campaign, with the latter opening their United Rugby Championship (URC) campaign at home against Cardiff on Saturday night (19:45 BST).

"Performing on the field is the only way we're going to get our fans here," said Davies.

"We can't expect them to turn up unless we're performing, so we appreciate that, but we'd love them to all turn up on Saturday.

"It's a huge game which sets the stall out for the rest of the season."

Davies also says he realises the importance of local Welsh derbies which would be eroded if a team was culled.

"The rivalry is the best bit, isn't it?" said Davies.

"When you play against the Ospreys, Cardiff and Dragons, that's fantastic and long may that continue because that means so much to people.

"We don't get great crowds at the URC because of the logistics of the league, but in those events we do get good crowds.

"There's a need for that. People want to come and see those local derbies that we still have."

Davies says any final decision on the make-up of Welsh professional rugby should not be based on the 2026-27 campaign.

"You just can't look at a moment in time in Welsh rugby," said Davies.

"People will judge now because of the situation, so we realise there's a role and responsibility there as well for us to perform.

"We're not oblivious to that, but let's not forget this is more than just a moment in time."

Davies pointed to areas of strength that he believes benefit the Scarlets.

"There's a history and a legacy from this place," said Davies.

"We've also got this Parc y Scarlets facility, which nobody else has got, and we've got probably one of the strongest boards in Welsh rugby.

"So there's a lot of stuff that historically supports the Scarlets."

Davies also pointed to the development of players in west Wales.

"You've got to look at where the players historically come from," he said.

"Ourselves and the Ospreys have probably been the two most successful in developing rugby players into becoming Welsh internationals. You can't ignore that.

"There's a reason for that. These are strong communities with strong rugby heritage, strong colleges and strong schools that play rugby and develop those players.

"There are hotbeds within Welsh rugby. As the game is shrinking all the time, those hotbeds are key and vital."

Davies says the Welsh game, particularly the pathway, has been damaged in recent years

"Over the decades, we've eroded a lot of what was good about our game. I'm struggling to see what's left," said Davies.

"Our pathway doesn't identify talent now until 16, and it's difficult for a young rugby player or the parents of young rugby player to see a pathway for a player right now.

"I look at other areas of the union, and the liability of what they're doing, what they're trying to do and the lack of anything being driven at this moment in time."

Davies returned as interim director of rugby halfway through last season above head coach Dwayne Peel, with Scarlets eventually finishing 14th in the URC out of 16.

He was installed in a permanent role during the summer.

"I'm old enough now to have learned the fact that you never say never," said Davies.

"I was sort of planning my semi-retirement, but once the opportunity came, I had absolutely no hesitation.

"I know I've come back in a far stronger position in my experience and knowledge and the work I've done in other organisations."

Davies, 61, says he has learned new things since returning to Scarlets.

"One of the things for me personally is just culturally, the group, the generation, how you engage with this group is different to how it's been previously," said Davies.

"It's a good thing. It brings diversity. We learn from each other and I've learned a lot of lessons.

"Some things I would have said previously probably aren't appropriate any more to say. I'm learning the triggers.

"It's been interesting and I've learned a lot myself over the last six months."

articles.title: Leigh Leopards and Wigan Warriors under RFL investigation over conduct
articles.summary: Leigh Leopards and Wigan Warriors are issued letters to inform them there will be an independent investigation into their conduct over the past 12 months.
articles.body:
Leigh Leopards and Wigan Warriors will face an independent investigation into their conduct over the past 12 months, the Rugby Football League has said.

The Super League play-off between the neighbouring clubs last October was overshadowed when Leopards owner Derek Beaumont said his side might boycott the fixture over a disagreement about their ticket allocation of 4,800.

The game ultimately went ahead as scheduled, with Wigan winning 18-6, but the Leopards submitted a complaint to the RFL the following week.

Wigan will host Wakefield in the play-off semi-final on Saturday and the Warriors released a statement last week to say whoever they played would receive an allocation of 5,000 tickets.

Trinity beat Leigh in their eliminator match, where a win for the opposition would have meant them progressing to face Wigan instead.

The RFL said in a statement: "The independent Rugby Football League and RL Commercial boards have issued a letter to both Leigh Leopards RLFC and Wigan Warriors RLFC advising them there will be an independent investigation into the conduct and actions of both clubs and the governing body in relation to matters extending over the last 12 months.

"The RFL and RL Commercial will not make any further comment until the investigation is complete."

BBC Sport has contacted both Leigh Leopards and Wigan Warriors for comment.

articles.title: Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan: The Wales captains looking to conquer England
articles.summary: Wales captains Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan prepare to make their Prem debuts for Gloucester after moving from Ospreys.
articles.body:
You might argue that for Welsh rugby to lose one Wales captain to an English club was unfortunate but two on the same day was just careless.

That is what happened in December 2025 when flanker Jac Morgan and hooker Dewi Lake announced they were leaving Ospreys for Gloucester for the 2026-27 season.

A two-for-one deal for the English club, who are investing in the Welsh duo to help turn their fortunes around.

Now the pair are preparing to make their Prem debuts against Exeter this Saturday.

Lake has been unveiled as the new Gloucester captain with Morgan as one of his deputies, demonstrating the favourable impression the pair have already made.

BBC Sport Wales caught up with them at their new Kingsholm home to talk about their early Gloucester experiences, leaving Ospreys and Welsh rugby politics behind and forgetting they are speaking Welsh in their new English environment.

Why are Wales' captains leaving for England?

Singleton hopes for return after heart attack

Losing Gloucester captaincy was 'brutal' - Ludlow

Home from home as Welsh influence continues

The duo have been almost inseparable since meeting a decade ago and were chosen as co-captains for the 2023 World Cup by former Wales coach Warren Gatland.

Lake is 27 and Morgan 26, with only eight months separating them.

Where one is, the other is never far behind, with Lake and Morgan having developed an almost telepathic understanding. They do not quite finish each other's sentences. But it is not far off.

The pair say they did not speak to each other about signing for Gloucester but fate has ensured they stay together in the next chapter of their rugby story.

"I am incredibly happy we got to land at the same club together," said Lake.

"We have come up together and spent 10 years day in, day out.

"He's an incredible friend off the field, but on the field also an incredible leader and player.

"Even the first day at Gloucester, we texted each other and said we'll meet at half past seven in the car park because neither of us wanted to go in on our own.

"To be able to get to see him day in day out and still spend time with him is incredible. I feel the bond we've created is really strong."

Lake described Gloucester as not too dissimilar to life in Wales, helped by a strong Welsh contingent of Max Llewellyn, Freddie Thomas, Josh Hathaway and Deian Gwynne who are already at Kingsholm.

Morgan agreed, saying: "It's been like a home from home. It's great to have a couple of fellow Welshmen here."

Not just fellow Welshmen but Welsh speakers, with Gwynne and Llewellyn comfortably conversing in their native language.

"A lot of us are speaking Welsh to each other when we're in the building," said Morgan.

"So it's been great to be able to do that. It's hard sometimes when you know someone can speak Welsh, it's hard to speak English to them!"

Lake added: "Jac and I rarely speak English to each other.

"We've got to catch ourselves and stop ourselves sometimes when other people are involved in conversations as well.

"In our first week we caught ourselves talking Welsh to each other at the breakfast table.

"We apologised and were forgetting we're not in Wales anymore, but we still speak Welsh to each other where we can."

No milk challenge as Gloucester welcome new boys

The duo are grateful the infamous Gloucester "milk challenge" initiation stopped before they joined.

New players used to have to finish eight pints of milk within a time limit of about 20 minutes without being sick.

The penalty for being sick or not finishing the challenge in time was having their head shaved.

"Jac and I spent the full summer on ChatGPT with pictures of ourselves bald just to start preparing ourselves."

It has been replaced by a more physical "shed challenge" that includes running up and down steps with sandbags and flipping tyres.

"Being here at Gloucester has been class so far," said Lake.

"The boys and coaches have been welcoming, it feels like a place where I'm able to get better, learn a lot and test my game in a new league.

"I wanted to challenge myself and be uncomfortable, if you like, in a new environment.

"That's the reason why I decided to make the move and I'm sure Jac feels the same."

Morgan says Gloucester being a traditional rugby city and community was a draw.

"A lot of people have been stopping us in the street and saying welcome to Gloucester," said Morgan.

"You can see how much this club means for the city and you sense the history.

"A lot of the boys mentioned 'the Shed' [Kingsholm stand], so it'll hopefully be a great experience to be able to play in front of the home crowd.

"We want to get a few more wins this year, do better than last year and see where it goes."

Morgan has also drawn on previous Welsh legends at Gloucester with Tomos Williams, James Hook and Richard Hibbard having previously played at Kingsholm.

"There's a lot of Welsh who have played here in the past and they're part of the history," said Morgan.

"There's a photo of Hibs [Hibbard] up in the corridors there, so it's good being able to see that.

"You speak to a lot of the past players about their experiences and Gloucester loved having them at the club."

Lake and Morgan join a sizeable Welsh contingent in English club rugby this season alongside the likes of Aaron Wainwright, Dafydd Jenkins, Rhys Carre, Nicky Smith, Tomas Francis, Tomos Williams and Louis Rees-Zammit.

Despite the excitement of their new life, Morgan and Lake are sad to leave Ospreys behind.

"We're both thankful of everything the Ospreys have given us over the last few years and the bonds we created with players and coaches," said Morgan.

"Probably the hardest part was leaving the people and you've got best mates back at home.

"We're still in contact with everybody but the lack of day-to-day contact is probably one of the hardest things to leave."

That passion includes paying to watch their old side.

"We still come in Mondays and the first thing we talk about is the Ospreys score on the weekend," said Lake.

"We both paid £5 the other night to watch them play against Coventry in a pre-season game.

"So the love for the club and people is still there with both of us and will not go away.

"It was a tough decision to leave, it was always going to be. Ospreys did everything for us, gave us an opportunity and platform and the chance to represent our country."

One thing they do not miss is the Welsh rugby politics, with Lake and Morgan signing for Gloucester at a time of uncertainty over whether Ospreys would survive beyond last season.

"The off-the-field stuff going on in background was tough to deal with sometimes," said Lake.

"It's nice to get away from it sometimes. It's one less thing to think about when you're playing here. It's easier for us to be here and not think of it.

"Over the last year or two, it's kind of dictated a lot that's gone on at the Ospreys, in terms of stuff we've had to do away from training and representing that region.

"It'll never be something we don't think about because we've still got friends there that will be affected by what is going on.

"We will try and catch up with the boys back home and still worry about them."

Since Morgan and Lake announced their Gloucester move, Ospreys have been given a stay of execution for at least two seasons.

But one of Ospreys or Scarlets are set to disappear by 2028 with a professional side in the west being cut by the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU).

"We don't have to deal with it but we still love the club and want Ospreys to be safe," said Lake.

"That's something we speak of and think about often."

Ospreys say WRU plan to cut team is wrong

WRU sticking to three-team plan - Reddin

Resilient Ospreys players need certainty - Jones

Wales moving in right direction with World Cup looming

Lake and Morgan are set to return to Wales for the Nations Championship in November.

A victory in the summer against Fiji was followed by away defeats against Argentina and South Africa, with home games against Japan, New Zealand and Australia to follow in the autumn.

Reflecting on the summer campaign, Lake said: "It was a mixed bag. The Argentina game was probably the most disappointing.

"We had enough talent in our tank to beat that team but we didn't make them work too hard and we let ourselves down.

"I still think it's a positive summer in terms of where we've been, compared to where we are now.

"We can see the the growth and the fact we're talking about we should have beaten Argentina.

"We wouldn't have been saying that two years ago."

A World Cup in Australia is on the horizon in a year's time but firstly the new life in Gloucester awaits. One Lake and Morgan will enjoy together.

articles.title: Newcastle: 'Start-up' side ready to tap into Red Bull spirit for new season
articles.summary: Head coach Dan McFarland is excited to have the backing of Newcastle Red Bulls' owners as he tries to fuse a new team together in the Prem this season.
articles.body:
It is all change at Newcastle Red Bulls as they prepare for the new Prem season, but they plan to tackle it with the sort of fearless approach for which their owners are renowned.

With Red Bull taking over at Kingston Park in August 2025, it was a scramble to get things in place for last season.

As a result, Newcastle could not bridge the gap to the other nine teams and finished bottom for a fourth successive campaign, with just two wins in 18 games.

But, after a huge influx of players in the summer, 'Red Bulls 2.0' under new head coach Dan McFarland are ready to embrace the challenge as they begin with a daunting trip to champions Northampton Saints on Friday night.

"It couldn't be set up any better for a spectacle for us," McFarland said. "The team starting at the back of the grid against the team on pole position.

"For us, it's a massive challenge and exactly the sort of thing a Red Bull team would relish going after, something that's hugely tough but really exciting to be involved in."

Englishman McFarland has returned home to head up that challenge after a successful spell in Japan as forwards coach at Kobelco Kobe Steelers.

The Red Bulls had three different head coaches last season with Steve Diamond, Alan Dickens and then Stephen Jones in charge but McFarland feels like the first proper appointment by the new ownership for this role.

"One of the reasons this was so attractive was trying to pull something together from scratch, basically being a start-up," he said.

Previously head coach at Ulster, the 54-year-old has got used to big business and rugby working together and he has tapped into the Red Bull organisation in his first few months on Tyneside.

Newcastle have recruited no fewer than 25 new players for this season so gelling that number of people together in a few weeks presents a significant obstacle.

But he reveals they benefited from a trip to the organisation's headquarters in Salzburg in Austria in pre-season to help a new playing squad gel and feel part of a wider family.

"Outside of Japan, big corporations don't get involved in rugby clubs," said McFarland.

"It's very rare, to have that backing but it's also the way Red Bull go into these kinds of ventures. It's not a feeling of 'let's see how it goes'. It's in with two feet and 'we've deliberately chosen you, Newcastle, because we believe we can do special things with you'.

"That is pretty special and they back it up with the support, the opportunities they offer for collaboration at different levels within the organisation - it could be for athlete performance teams, elite athletes and definitely in marketing."

After their opener at Northampton, Newcastle then face two other play-off sides from last season - a home game with Leicester Tigers and a trip to Exeter Chiefs - in the opening three-week block of league fixtures.

It is not an easy start, but McFarland likens Newcastle's challenge in the Prem this season to that undertaken by Red Bull's F1 driver Max Verstappen as he raced behind 100 amateur drivers in a go-kart race at Silverstone earlier this month - slightly eccentric but one that gets the juices flowing.

"We look at it like this, we're starting at the back of the grid and we've got all these teams ahead of us," he said.

"Let's see if we can pick them off and we're going to have fun trying to do it."
